hypotheses.title: Narrowing-chain walks make stage-5 type resolution O(N^2) when a local is repeatedly reassigned and re-narrowed
hypotheses.issue: Stage 5 (local type resolution) is O(N^2) in the number of statements of a function when a local is repeatedly reassigned and re-narrowed, e.g. `v = get(i); if v is () { return; } else { c += v; }` repeated N times. In semantics/internal/types/type_resolver_narrowing.go each assignment to a narrowed local pushes an unnarrowing entry onto the narrowing `binding` chain (unnarrowSymbolAt), and each type test's surviving branch narrowing is pushed too (narrowByType, mergeStatementEffects / mergeChains), so the chain grows by ~2-3 entries per statement and is never cut. Every variable reference then walks that chain all the way to nil: (1) canNarrow scans every entry looking for capture entries (isCaptureEntry + CaptureGroupContains) for each mutable local, even when the function has no loops/lambdas and therefore no capture entries at all (41% cum CPU, isCaptureEntry 30% flat); (2) lookupBindingInner walks the full chain for every reference to a variable that has no binding on the chain (e.g. `c` in `c += v`) (~25% cum); (3) mergeChains -> commonAncestor -> chainDepth counts both chains to nil at every if/else join although they diverge only 1-2 entries up. Callers: resolveSimpleVarRef, resolveCompoundAssignment, unnarrowSymbolAt, resolveTypeTestExpr. This is distinct from the earlier loop/lambda capture-entry reports: here there are no loops, lambdas or capture entries; the cost is pure chain length.

hypotheses.fix_approach: Cache a per-node summary of the chain beneath each binding, computed once at construction through a single constructor newBinding (bindings are immutable after creation, so summaries stay valid): depth (chainDepth becomes O(1), so commonAncestor/mergeChains cost is proportional to divergence), nearestCapture (pointer to closest capture entry at or below; canNarrow and capture checks hop only over capture entries and do nothing when there are none), and refMask, a 64-bit bloom-style mask of refs bound at or below the node (if the ref's bit is clear, no entry binds it, so lookupBindingInner skips straight to a capture-only check that reproduces the old walk's result: unnarrowedSymbol(ref) if a capture group contains it and the decl is not final/param, else ref). Pitfalls: every &binding{...} literal (in type_resolver_narrowing.go and type_resolver.go: lambda boundaries, resolveDefaultExpression, aggregateQueryVariable, match-clause narrowing, singletonResultEffect, mergeChains) must go through the constructor or summaries are wrong; the mask is only a negative filter (false positives fall back to the full walk). A cleaner production fix might instead cut/compact shadowed entries per statement, but the summary approach is behaviour-preserving and passed make test unchanged.
